newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila to absorb former foes into new Congo army.
newsitem.headline: Kabila to absorb former foes into new Congo army.

text.p: Ousted Zairean dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's troops are to be trained and absorbed into the new Congolese army of President Laurent Kabila, state radio said on Wednesday.

It said the soldiers, who barely put up a fight as Kabila's rebels marched across the country in a seven-month rebellion, were being sent from the capital Kinshasa to Kitona, 360 km (240 miles) to the southeast, for initial training.
It is unclear which units of the ex-government army will join the reunified national force that is to be formed soon.
"The ex-army soldiers are to receive intensive training in the military base of Kitona. I don't know how long for," said one of Mobutu's captains who declined to be named.
"I have decided to follow a business career. I have been humiliated as a military man," he told Reuters.
Kabila grabbed power in May and renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Mobutu's poorly paid and demoralised troops were more inclined to loot than fight. Their senior officers, widely seen as Mobutu cronies, fled the country before the arrival of Kabila's forces in Kinshasa.
"The ex-army soldiers have been asked to hand in their weapons. The deadline has passed now," the radio said.
State television read out a communique which suggested that "arrest and prosecution" awaited members of the disbanded army who refused to go to Kitona.
